title: The Last Supper and Betrayal
overview: Luke 22 presents a pivotal moment in the Gospel narrative, detailing Jesus' final hours before His crucifixion. The chapter begins with the plotting of Jesus' betrayal, followed by the institution of the Lord’s Supper, where Jesus establishes a new covenant through His body and blood. It highlights themes of servanthood, faithfulness, and the coming suffering of Christ. The chapter also records Jesus’ prayer in Gethsemane, His arrest, Peter’s denial, and Jesus’ initial trial before the Jewish leaders. This chapter is crucial as it sets the theological foundation for the passion, emphasizing Jesus’ willing sacrifice and the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy.
structure:
**Verses 1-6: The Plot to Betray Jesus.** The chief priests and scribes conspire to kill Jesus, fearing the people’s reaction, while Satan enters Judas, who agrees to betray Jesus for money.

**Verses 7-38: The Last Supper and Teachings.** Jesus instructs Peter and John to prepare the Passover. He institutes the Lord’s Supper, symbolizing His body and blood as the new covenant. Jesus teaches about humility and servanthood, foretells Peter’s denial, and prepares His disciples for the coming trials.

**Verses 39-46: Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives.** Jesus prays earnestly, submitting to the Father’s will despite the agony, while His disciples struggle to stay awake and pray.

**Verses 47-53: The Arrest of Jesus.** Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss, leading to His arrest. Jesus heals the ear of the high priest’s servant, rebukes the violent response, and acknowledges the spiritual darkness of the hour.

**Verses 54-62: Peter’s Denial.** Peter follows Jesus at a distance but denies Him three times as Jesus predicted, fulfilling Jesus’ warning and highlighting human weakness.

**Verses 63-71: Jesus Before the Council.** Jesus is mocked and questioned by the Jewish leaders about His identity, affirming His Messiahship and divine authority despite their rejection.

keyVerses.text: And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
keyVerses.significance: This verse institutes the Lord’s Supper, a foundational Christian ordinance symbolizing Jesus’ sacrificial death. It emphasizes remembrance and the new covenant established through His body.

keyVerses.text: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.
keyVerses.significance: Here Jesus declares the cup as the new covenant sealed by His blood, pointing to the atoning sacrifice that brings forgiveness and reconciliation with God.

keyVerses.text: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
keyVerses.significance: Jesus warns Peter of spiritual attack, illustrating the reality of spiritual warfare and the need for perseverance and prayer in faith.

keyVerses.text: Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
keyVerses.significance: This prayer reveals Jesus’ submission to the Father’s will despite His anguish, modeling obedience and trust in God’s redemptive plan.

keyVerses.text: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
keyVerses.significance: This moment of recognition brings Peter to repentance, highlighting human frailty and the possibility of restoration through Christ’s grace.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: The Son of God and central figure of the chapter, who institutes the Lord’s Supper, prays in Gethsemane, faces betrayal and arrest, and affirms His identity before the Jewish leaders. His actions reveal His obedience, love, and fulfillment of prophecy.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.description: One of the twelve disciples who becomes the betrayer by conspiring with the chief priests and agreeing to hand Jesus over for money. His actions set in motion the events leading to Jesus’ arrest.

characters.name: Peter
characters.description: A leading disciple who is warned by Jesus about spiritual attack. Despite his bold declarations, he denies Jesus three times, fulfilling Jesus’ prophecy and demonstrating human weakness and the need for forgiveness.

characters.name: Chief Priests and Scribes
characters.description: Religious leaders who plot to kill Jesus out of fear of the people and to maintain their authority. They orchestrate His arrest and trial, representing opposition to Jesus’ mission.

characters.name: Satan
characters.description: The spiritual adversary who enters Judas, influencing him to betray Jesus. Satan’s role underscores the cosmic battle over Jesus’ mission and the forces opposing God’s kingdom.

themes.description: This chapter highlights betrayal through Judas and Peter’s denial, showing the frailty of human loyalty and the reality of sin even among Jesus’ closest followers. It points to the need for grace and restoration.
The institution of the Lord’s Supper reveals Jesus’ impending sacrifice as the basis for the new covenant. His body broken and blood shed signify the atonement for sin, central to Christian faith.
Jesus teaches that true greatness is found in serving others, contrasting worldly power with kingdom values. This theme prepares the disciples for the suffering and service expected of them.
Jesus’ prayer in Gethsemane models submission to God’s will amid suffering, encouraging believers to trust God even in trials and to seek strength through prayer.
The chapter reveals the reality of spiritual opposition, with Satan seeking to sift the disciples like wheat. It underscores the need for vigilance, prayer, and faithfulness.

historicalContext: This chapter is set in Jerusalem during the Jewish festival of Passover, a time commemorating Israel’s deliverance from Egypt. The city was under Roman occupation, with religious leaders holding significant authority but also fearing unrest among the people. The Passover meal was a sacred tradition involving the sacrifice of a lamb and a communal meal, which Jesus reinterprets to signify His impending sacrifice. The political and religious tensions of the time created a volatile environment, with the Sanhedrin seeking to eliminate Jesus as a perceived threat to their power and the fragile peace with Rome.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in the events of this chapter, viewing Jesus’ sacrifice as the fulfillment of covenant promises. The Lord’s Supper is seen as a means of grace, a memorial of Christ’s atoning work and a spiritual nourishment for believers.

Dispensationalists highlight the prophetic fulfillment in Jesus’ passion and the distinction between Israel and the Church. They often interpret the Lord’s Supper as a symbolic ordinance pointing forward to Christ’s future kingdom.

Early Church Fathers like Augustine and Chrysostom focus on the spiritual significance of the Lord’s Supper as participation in Christ’s body and blood, and on Jesus’ prayer as an example of perfect obedience and submission to the Father.

crossReferences.connection: Paul’s account of the Lord’s Supper echoes Jesus’ institution in Luke 22, emphasizing remembrance and proclamation of Christ’s death.
Parallel account of Jesus’ prayer in Gethsemane, highlighting His submission and the disciples’ weakness.
Jesus teaches servanthood by washing the disciples’ feet, complementing His teaching on humility in Luke 22.
Prophecy of the suffering servant, fulfilled in Jesus being 'reckoned among the transgressors' as mentioned in Luke 22:37.
Prophecy about betrayal by a close friend, fulfilled in Judas’ actions.
Prophecy about the shepherd being struck and the sheep scattering, fulfilled in Jesus’ arrest and the disciples’ flight.

application: Remember and participate regularly in the Lord’s Supper as a proclamation of Christ’s sacrifice and a means of grace.
Emulate Christ’s humility by serving others selflessly, rejecting worldly notions of greatness.
Remain vigilant in prayer, especially during trials, seeking God’s strength and submitting to His will.
Recognize the reality of spiritual warfare and guard your faith through prayer and reliance on God.
Confess and repent quickly when you fail, trusting in God’s forgiveness and restoration.
Stand firm in faith even when facing opposition or betrayal, knowing God’s sovereign plan prevails.
conclusion: Luke 22 powerfully captures the tension and solemnity of Jesus’ final hours before His crucifixion. Through the institution of the Lord’s Supper, Jesus establishes the foundation of Christian worship and the new covenant of grace. His teachings on humility and servanthood challenge believers to embody kingdom values. The chapter’s portrayal of prayer, betrayal, denial, and trial reveals the depth of Jesus’ obedience and the frailty of human faith, yet also points to God’s redemptive purpose. For believers today, this chapter calls for faithful remembrance, humble service, vigilant prayer, and trust in Christ’s victorious sacrifice.
timeline: c. AD 30 - The Passion Week in Jerusalem

A covenant or agreement; in Luke 22:20, it refers to the new covenant established by Jesus’ blood.
To separate or test by shaking; here, Satan desires to test the disciples’ faith like wheat being sifted.
A vessel used in the Passover meal; symbolically represents the suffering and blood of Christ in the new covenant.
A room prepared for guests, specifically the upper room where Jesus and His disciples ate the Passover.
